title: Model Retirement and Decommissioning: Regulatory Obligations Under EU AI Act and GDPR — Council of AI Operational Guide
context: 2026-08-31 engine cycle — When an AI model reaches end-of-life, the regulatory question shifts from 'is it safe to deploy?' to 'did you decommission it properly?' The EU AI Act (Article 17, Article 61), GDPR (Article 17 right to erasure, Article 35 DPIA for decommissioning risk), and the EU Cyber Resilience Act all impose distinct obligations on model retirement. This seed page maps those obligations to the Council of AI measurement board so operators have an auditable trail.
body: Model decommissioning is the most neglected phase of the AI lifecycle — and increasingly the most regulated. Three intersecting obligations create liability if handled incorrectly. First, the EU AI Act Article 17 (quality management system) requires providers to document the entire lifecycle, including decommissioning, as part of ongoing conformity assessment. If a high-risk model is retired without documenting what it was connected to, what data it held, and what downstream systems depended on it, the QMS record is incomplete — and the notified body audit will flag it. Second, GDPR Article 17 (right to erasure) applies when model weights encode personal data — which nearly all fine-tuned models do. Decommissioning is not deleting the checkpoint file. It is demonstrating that no inference endpoint, cached embedding, downstream LoRA adapter, or vector-database index still retains contaminated parameters. The Council of AI privacy axis ('prv') measures exactly this: whether a model can be probed for residual training-data memorisation after decommissioning procedures. A post-decommissioning measurement showing non-zero memorisation is evidence of incomplete erasure. Third, the Cyber Resilience Act (CRA, fully applicable 2027) treats model endpoints as products with digital elements: a decommissioned model that remains reachable on an unmaintained endpoint is a known-vulnerability liability. The vendor must issue a decommissioning notice, patch or remove the endpoint, and maintain a vulnerability disclosure record for two years post-decommissioning. The Council of AI measurement board provides the audit trail for all three obligations: (a) the 'prv' axis certifies that post-decommissioning probes show zero memorisation above the measurement instrument noise floor; (b) the 'det' axis confirms that downstream detector-interoperability tests show the endpoint has been sealed or removed; (c) the Containment Incident Index logs the decommissioning event with a signed timestamp, producing an immutable record that the model was retired on a specific date with specific measured outcomes. Operational workflow: before decommissioning, run a full 14-axis GSPC measurement sweep on the model; sign the sweep record; publish it to the Containment Incident Index as a retirement record; archive both the model weights and the signed sweep for the retention period (10 years for high-risk AI systems under EU AI Act Article 11 Annex IV). If a regulator asks three years later whether the model was retired cleanly, the operator pulls the signed measurement record and verifies it offline — no reliance on the original vendor, no expired API keys, no lost logs.
